core_obligations: Propagate the flat-base-change property from M-underlined and L to G by the five lemma, and deduce the weight decomposition of G over graded algebras (proof lines 788-796).
Present L by a matrix and construct the graded algebra B together with the element xi whose orbit map is an isomorphism onto L (proof lines 798-815).
Use the weight decomposition to lift xi to an element theta of G(B), (proof lines 817-823).
Construct the graded algebra C with the maps p_1, p_2, m, form tau and show tau lies in M tensor_A C_1 (proof lines 825-849).
Conclude from the vanishing of tau that G is adequate (proof lines 849-884).
proof_roadmap: Flat base change and the weight decomposition (proof lines 788-796).
Presentation of L and the element xi (proof lines 798-815).
The test algebra C and the element tau (proof lines 825-849).
difficulty_reason: For a ring A and a short exact sequence 0 -> M-underlined -> G -> L -> 0 of module-valued functors with L linearly adequate, the lemma asserts that G is adequate (statement lines 780-786). The proof first propagates the flat-base-change property to G by the five lemma, so that G splits as the direct sum of its weight spaces over any graded A-algebra; it then chooses a presentation of L and exhibits a graded algebra B and an element xi of L(B) whose orbit map is an isomorphism onto L, lifts xi to theta in G(B) via the weight decomposition, builds the graded algebra C with its three algebra maps p_1, p_2, m, and shows that tau = G(m)(theta) - G(p_1)(theta) - G(p_2)(theta) lies in M tensor C_1; the remainder of the proof uses this to conclude that G is adequate (proof lines 788-884). The level is H3: a long construction with a non-obvious choice of test algebra and an explicit element chase.
